podcast.body: An anthemic 1981 duet with Queen, widely considered a masterpiece for both artists. It reached number one in the UK and got Bowie back into the US Top 40 (peaking at number 28) for the first time in six years. Featuring explosive vocals by Freddie Mercury, an "immortal baseline" by John Deacon (later sampled by Vanilla Ice for "Ice Ice Baby"), and lyrics primarily written by Bowie, it's described as a song of protest, fellowship, and love. "We've talked about under pressure, David Bowie's Anthemic 1981 duet with the band Queen in several prior hit parade episodes."

podcast.body: The dramatic 1981 duet between British rock legends Queen and David Bowie, which peaked in the US at a modest number 29 in early 1982. Its iconic baseline was famously sampled and became the foundation for Vanilla Ice's 1990 number one hit "Ice Ice Baby." "the dramatic 1981 duet Under Pressure by British rock legends Queen and David Bowie."
